priority_assessment.reason: The manuscript is explicitly framed as Hurufi-Bektashi and co-locates Hakiki with Hatai and Nesimi, matching the strongest co-occurrence profile of the verified Diyarbakir/Ilkhchi Alevi Hakiki witnesses. It remains unverified because no Hakiki incipit, folio, image, or item count is published.

source.title: Abdulla Rexhepi and Zeqije Xhafce, Exploring Hurufi-Bektashi Sufism in Albanian Literature. Insights from an Old Manuscript
published_pdf_evidence_notes: Article section describing the Millet Library / Ali Emiri manuscript identification, page extent, language distribution, and old/new registration numbers.
Article author-roster passage naming Hakiki together with Nesimi and Hatai in the Turkish/Persian section.

why_it_matters: This is an open-web Balkan Hurufi-Bektashi cenk/conk lead with Hakiki co-listed with Hatai and Nesimi in a manuscript explicitly framed as Hurufi-Bektashi. It is outside the already-known Diyarbakir, Ilkhchi/Kirklar, and Sivas/Anatolia fieldwork cluster.
limits: The article does not publish the Hakiki poem, incipit, explicit, folio, or image.
The unqualified Hakiki author name could be Cihan Shah, Yusuf Hakiki, Agazade Mehmed Dede, a local Bektashi/Hurufi namesake, or a catalogue/author-roster simplification.
Bektashi/Hurufi Albanian transmission is adjacent to Alevi-Bektashi ritual manuscript culture, but this article does not prove current Alevi cem use.
The Millet/Ali Emiri shelfmark and catalogue record still need direct library/YEK verification.
next_verification_steps: Resolve the modern Millet Library catalogue record for old no. 551 / new no. 003094 and capture exact collection/shelfmark fields.
Request or inspect the Turkish/Persian section pages containing Hakiki.
Record folio/page, heading, incipit, explicit/mahlas line, meter, neighboring poems, and image status.
Collate any Hakiki text against Sohrabiabad-Akin 2019, Macit/Cihan Shah, Yusuf Hakiki, Agazade Mehmed Dede, and local Bektashi/Hurufi comparanda.
